newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks tumble in spillover from Slovenia.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks tumble in spillover from Slovenia.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks tumbled in sparse trade on Wednesday in what market watchers saw as a spillover from neighbouring Slovenia, where the central bank decided this week to tighten controls on foreign investment.
Croatia imposes no restrictions for foreign portfolio investors, but their reaction was said to be clearly linked to Slovenian developments.
"Foreigners investing in Slovenia and Croatia are the same. They react in the same way and are now withdrawing buy orders," said Marijan Palic of Auctor brokerage.
Eight of 11 active stocks fell and three were flat as only few selected issues resisted what appeared at first sight to be a general downward slide.
However, traders hoped the current jitters would not last although trade might suffer in the short term.
"It would be nice and it's not excluded that the capital intended for Slovenia ends up in Croatia instead," said Palic.
"I expect small volume, but I doubt sellers will lower the prices. In the end there will be stabilisation," he added.
On Wednesday, volume shrank to 7,875 units and turnover to 3.9 million kuna from Tuesday's 8.3 million.
Most actively traded issue was food concern Podravka, closing five kuna lower at 330 on volume of 3,376 units.
Hotelier Istraturist led decliners, falling 30 kuna or 12.2 percent to 215 kuna with 199 shares sold.
Blue chip Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries lost 2.12 percent to 1,850 kuna on volume of 61.
Another fully-listed issue, drugs firm Pliva, ended unchanged at 470 kuna with 556 shares sold.

The other two which held their ground were hotelier Laguna, at 1,500 kuna on a large volume of 1,008 shares, and Zagrebacka's C-series bearer stock at 900 kuna, though with no more than 17 units changing hands.
